title: Merchant status and the particular UCC provision
shortTitle: Merchant status and the particular UCC provision
summary: A merchant is a person whose dealings, occupation, or attributed professional knowledge meet the UCC’s definition for the provision being applied.
notes:
The inquiry can concern expertise in particular goods, business practices, or both. The casebook warns that the relevant kind of knowledge depends on the rule. For example, firm offers and the addition of terms between merchants have requirements that should be read with § 2-104. A business buying equipment for its own use cannot be classified merely by asking whether it resells that equipment. Conversely, Article 2 can apply to a sale involving a consumer even though a merchant-only rule does not.

The firm-offer notes distinguish expertise in goods from expertise in business practices. Section 2-207’s special incorporation rule applies between merchants; a nonmerchant’s receipt of an added term instead raises a proposal-and-assent question. A business buying equipment for its own use is not classified solely by whether it resells that product. Hill also warns that later commercial use of retail software does not by itself establish software-merchant status.
